The root cause of INC-4102 was that a deployment increased the number of replicas of the payments service from four to nine, which exceeded the database's connection ceiling. Each replica opens its own pool, and since the per-service connection ceiling is enforced at the database, the ninth replica's connections were refused, leading to the saturation of the connection pool and the subsequent failure of payment authorisation.

This issue was exacerbated by the fact that the replica count and connection ceiling are owned by different teams and reviewed in different meetings, with no mechanism in the deployment pipeline to compare the two. Additionally, the alert that fired was on authorisation failure rate, and the 80% alert that was added after INC-2451 did not cover the 100% utilisation that occurred before any customer was affected.

For more detailed information, you can refer to document [4] in the postmortem of INC-3187, which provides a comprehensive explanation of the events leading up to the incident.
